subtitle: A queen’s resolve against an emperor’s last march

panels.shot: low-angle medium-wide of a lone queen on a Deccan hilltop, dark Mughal encampments stretching in the distant plain
panels.action: Maharani Tarabai Mohite stands in regal armour over a plain cotton sari, one hand on a map-weighted table, the other on the parapet of a hill-fort, as storm clouds gather over a vast Mughal camp below.

dialogue.text: In the last harsh years of Aurangzeb’s Deccan war, Maharani Tarabai Mohite held a broken kingdom together and outlasted an empire’s fury.

i18n.hi: दक्खन की खूनखराबे भरी लड़ाइयों में, महारानी तराबाई मोहिटे ने टूटी मराठा सत्ता संभाली और साम्राज्य की आग से लंबी चलीं।

panels.shot: slow push-in from wide court view to three-quarter of Tarabai seated beside an empty throne
panels.action: In the audience hall of a besieged Satara, Tarabai sits beside the empty throne draped in saffron cloth, her young son’s small seat set slightly behind her, courtiers tense as news-bearing riders kneel at a distance.

dialogue.text: In 1700, as Mughal armies pressed the Deccan and fort after fort fell, Rajaram died at Sinhagad, leaving behind his widow Tarabai and a child-heir in a kingdom that seemed about to dissolve.

i18n.hi: १७०० में, जब मुगल फ़ौजें दक्खन को कुचल रही थीं और किले गिर रहे थे, सिंहगढ़ पर राजाराम की मौत हुई, पीछे छूटे उनकी रानी तराबाई, एक नन्हा वारिस, और बिखरता राज्य।

panels.shot: close-up on Tarabai’s face in three-quarter profile, background blurred courtiers and a child’s silhouette
panels.action: Tarabai leans slightly forward on the throne’s arm, jaw set, eyes steady, while the faint outline of her small son playing with a wooden horse shows behind her in soft focus.

dialogue.text: Daughter of Hambirrao Mohite, trained among soldiers and scribes, she knew forts, campaigns and accounts. Now, as regent for her son Shivaji II, she faced the emperor Aurangzeb at the height of his power.

i18n.hi: हंबीरराव मोहिटे की बेटी, सिपहियों और क़लमकारों के बीच पली–बढ़ी, उसे किले, मोर्चे और हिशाब सब याद थे। अब बेटे शिवाजी द्वितीय की संरक्षक बनकर, वो औरंगज़ेब से आर–पार भिड़ी, उस वक्त जब सम्राट सबसे ताक़तवर था।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye view of a map table littered with pebbles and figurines, Tarabai’s hand rearranging them
panels.action: Over a rough parchment map of the Deccan, Tarabai’s bangled hand moves small wooden horsemen toward the north, while ministers and sardars ring the table, some anxious, some defiant.

dialogue.text: Tarabai did not dream of one great battle. She chose endurance. Raids instead of pitched wars, shifting capitals instead of a single doomed seat, many commanders instead of one fragile hero.

i18n.hi: तराबाई किसी एक महा–युद्ध का सपना नहीं देखती थी। उसने चुना धैर्य को — धावा, न कि खुली लड़ाई; बदलती राजनियाँ, न कि एक ही किले पर दाँव; कई सेनानायक, न कि एक अकेला नायक।

panels.shot: wide shot inside a fort courtyard, Tarabai addressing assembled sardars
panels.action: In a torchlit fort courtyard, cloaked against the night breeze, Tarabai stands on a stone step, addressing a circle of armoured sardars who rest their hands on sword-hilts and spear shafts.

dialogue.speaker: maharani_tarabai_mohite
dialogue.text: We will not meet him head-on. We will make his empire bleed by distance and time.

i18n.hi: हम सीधी टक्कर नहीं देंगे। हम उसके साम्राज्य को दूरी और वक़्त से लहूलुहान करेंगे।

panels.shot: epic wide landscape of the Deccan with multiple small vignettes of moving Maratha forces
panels.action: A sweeping view of the Deccan plateau shows small columns of Maratha horsemen threading through thorny scrub, another detachment slipping past a village temple, and distant smoke from a plundered Mughal supply camp on the horizon.

dialogue.text: From hill-fort councils she sent out trusted commanders. They harried imperial outposts, cut grain convoys, struck into Berar and Khandesh, then vanished into the scrub and ghats before the Mughals could strike back.

i18n.hi: पहाड़ी किलों की सभाओं से उसने भरोसेमंद सरदार भेजे। उन्होंने मुग़ल चौकियाँ झकझोड़ीं, अनाज के काफ़िले लूटे, बेऱार और ख़ानदेश तक धावे बोले, फिर झाड़ियों और घाटों में ग़ायब हो गए, इससे पहले कि मुग़ल पलटवार कर सकें।

panels.shot: contrast panel split diagonally: one half showing exhausted Mughal camp, other half Maratha campfire planning
panels.action: On one side, a sprawling Mughal camp at dusk lies heavy with tired soldiers and tethered elephants; on the other, under a smaller fire, Maratha officers bend over letters and palm-leaf records, planning the next foray.

dialogue.text: Khafi Khan, writing from the imperial side, lamented how Maratha bands cut loose across the land. Tarabai’s orders turned scattered resistance into policy, forcing Aurangzeb to chase shadows from fort to fort.

i18n.hi: ख़फ़ी ख़ाँ ने, बादशाह की तरफ़ से लिखते हुए, रोया कि मराठा टोलियाँ हर तरफ़ आज़ाद घूम रहीं। तराबाई के हुक्मों ने बिखरे विरोध को नीति बना दिया, औरंगज़ेब को किले–किले भटकते साये का पीछा करने पर मजबूर किया।

panels.shot: interior medium shot of Tarabai with scribes and clerks, focus on documents and seals
panels.action: Inside a modest but orderly chamber, Tarabai sits at a low desk, listening as a scribe reads a report; piles of farman copies, revenue lists and sealed letters lie neatly arranged before her.

dialogue.text: Her strength lay not only in war. She kept an administration alive in fragments—appointing revenue officers, confirming village headmen, granting jagirs to loyal chiefs—so that the Maratha state existed even when its cities were dust.

i18n.hi: उसकी ताक़त सिर्फ़ तलवार नहीं थी। उसने टूटी–फूटी ज़मीन पर भी शासन ज़िंदा रखा—मामलेदार लगाए, गाँव के मुखियों की पुष्टि की, वफ़ादार सरदारों को जागीरें बाँटी—ताकि मराठा राज्य जिए, चाहे शहर खंडहर हो गए हों।

panels.shot: medium-wide shot of Tarabai and her son in a moving palanquin, background showing a fort receding
panels.action: Tarabai rides in an open palanquin, veiled but alert, her young son beside her clutching a small shield, as attendants move along a narrow track; behind them, a hill-fort’s silhouette shrinks against the evening sky.

dialogue.text: She shifted court from fort to fort—Satara, Panhala, and the hill strongholds of the Western Ghats—keeping her son close, turning the royal household itself into a moving symbol that the kingdom still lived.

i18n.hi: वो दरबार को किले–किले घुमाती रही—सातारा, पन्हाला, और पश्चिमी घाट के गढ़—बेटे को साथ रखते हुए, खुद राजघराने को ही चलते–फिरते निशान में बदल दिया कि राज अब भी साँस ले रहा है।

panels.shot: expansive map-like bird’s-eye over central India, with stylised arrows towards Malwa and Gujarat
panels.action: A stylised view of central India shows slender saffron-tinted arrows sweeping from the Deccan northwest into Malwa and Gujarat, with small Maratha riders sketched atop them against a faint grid of rivers and towns.

dialogue.text: Under her regency, Maratha raids pushed farther. Bands reached into Malwa and even Gujarat, testing imperial frontiers, drawing Mughal garrisons away from the Deccan, and proving that the war had escaped Aurangzeb’s control.

i18n.hi: उसकी हुकूमत में मराठा धावे और दूर तक बढ़े। दल मलवा, यहाँ तक कि गुजरात तक जा पहुँचे, मुगल सरहदें परखी, दक्खन से गरिसनें खींचीं, और दिखा दिया कि अब जंग औरंगज़ेब के बस से बाहर है।

panels.shot: intimate interior of Aurangzeb’s tent, low-angle on the aging emperor over maps
panels.action: In a large but sparsely furnished tent near Ahmadnagar, an aged Aurangzeb bends over crumpled maps and reports by lamplight, beads in his fingers, lines of fatigue etched deep on his face.

dialogue.text: By the time the emperor turned seventy, his armies were worn thin by years in the field. He sat in his tent near Ahmadnagar, far from Delhi, writing anxious letters while Maratha horsemen slipped through his lines.

i18n.hi: जब सम्राट सत्तर के पार पहुँचा, उसकी फ़ौजें सालों की मुहिम से घिस चुकी थीं। अहमदनगर के पास डेरा डाले, वो दिल्ली से दूर, टेंट में बैठा घबराए ख़त लिख रहा था, जबकि मराठा सवार उसकी पंक्तियों में से सरक जाते थे।

panels.shot: still, solemn shot of a bier leaving a Mughal camp, soldiers bowing their heads
panels.action: At dawn outside the Ahmadnagar camp, Mughal officers and soldiers bow their heads as a simple covered bier is carried slowly past rows of motionless tents and silent artillery.

dialogue.text: In 1707, Aurangzeb died in the Deccan, far from the capital he had ruled. His death did not bring peace. It freed rival princes and commanders to fight for Delhi, while Maratha commanders watched and weighed their chances.

i18n.hi: १७०७ में औरंगज़ेब दक्खन में मरा, उस राजधानी से कोसों दूर जिसे वो चलाता था। उसकी मौत से सुकून नहीं आया; बल्कि शहज़ादों और अमीरों के हाथ खुल गए, जो अब दिल्ली के लिए लड़ पड़े, और मराठा सरदार दूर खड़े मौक़े तौलने लगे।

panels.shot: medium shot of Tarabai receiving the news, balanced between stern resolve and quiet relief
panels.action: Tarabai stands in a fort balcony as a breathless messenger kneels before her; beyond, the dry hills stretch under a hard sun as a faint wind lifts the edge of her veil.

dialogue.speaker: maharani_tarabai_mohite
dialogue.text: An emperor has died. Our duty has not.

i18n.hi: एक सम्राट चला गया है। हमारा फ़र्ज़ अभी नहीं।

panels.shot: wide court scene in the north, Mughal noble presenting a letter of release to Shahu
panels.action: In an elegant northern hall, a Mughal noble bows as he presents a formal letter to a dignified Maratha captive, Shahu, who stands flanked by a few attendants but still bears the posture of a prince.

dialogue.text: To weaken Tarabai’s camp, the new powers in Delhi released Shahu, son of Sambhaji, held long in Mughal custody. His return to the Deccan carried chains of a different kind—claims, memories and rival loyalties.

i18n.hi: तराबाई का असर काटने को, दिल्ली के नए हाकिमों ने शंभाजी के बेटे शाहू को छोड़ा, जो बरसों मुगल कैद में था। उसका दक्खन लौटना नई ज़ंजीरें लाया—दावे, यादें और बँटी हुई वफ़ादारियाँ।

panels.shot: tense medium-wide of Tarabai in council, some sardars whispering to each other
panels.action: Back in the Deccan, Tarabai sits upright in council as news of Shahu’s march is announced; a few sardars whisper together at the edge of the hall, torn between old allegiances and present power.

dialogue.text: Tarabai claimed regency in the name of Shivaji II, son of Rajaram. Shahu claimed his father’s legacy as senior line. Sardars and village chiefs weighed which claimant could best protect their lands and honours.

i18n.hi: तराबाई ने राजाराम के बेटे शिवाजी द्वितीय के नाम पर खुद को संरक्षक बताया। शाहू ने अपने पिता शंभाजी की बड़ी लाइन का हक़ माँगा। सरदार और पाटिल तौलते रहे कि किस दावेदार से उनकी ज़मीन और इज़्ज़त ज़्यादा सुरक्षित रहेगी।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Tarabai in profile, shadows around her, a small Kolhapur map before her
panels.action: Tarabai, lit by a single oil lamp, studies a smaller map marked around Kolhapur, her profile calm but her eyes hard, as if accepting a narrower but still vital field of rule.

dialogue.speaker: maharani_tarabai_mohite
dialogue.text: If Satara chooses another, we will build from Kolhapur.

i18n.hi: अगर सातारा किसी और को चुनेगा, तो हम कोल्हापुर से अपना रास्ता बनाएँगे।

panels.shot: dynamic but non-violent wide shot of opposing Maratha forces near Khed, banners facing each other
panels.action: On an open field near Khed, two Maratha hosts stand facing each other at a wary distance, their standards—one bearing Shahu’s emblem, the other Tarabai’s line—fluttering in the dry wind as cavalry lines shift uneasily.

dialogue.text: In 1708, near Khed, Shahu’s forces met those loyal to Tarabai; the struggle turned on chiefs’ support as much as on lances. Shahu emerged stronger around Satara, while Tarabai drew back to Kolhapur.

i18n.hi: १७०८ में, खेड़ के पास, शाहू की फ़ौजें तराबाई वफ़ादारों से भिड़ीं; लड़ाई उतनी ही सरदारों की निष्ठा पर टिकी थी, जितनी भालों पर। शाहू सातारा पर मज़बूत हुआ, तराबाई कोल्हापुर लौट आई।

panels.shot: serene interior of a smaller Kolhapur court, Tarabai presiding over a petition
panels.action: In a more modest yet orderly hall at Kolhapur, Tarabai sits on a simple throne, hearing a village headman’s petition, while a clerk records her decision and a young officer watches with respect.

dialogue.text: Defeated at Khed but not erased, she ruled at Kolhapur, issuing orders, managing land grants, and shaping a rival court that continued the line of Rajaram, even as Shahu’s Satara became the more famous centre.

i18n.hi: खेड़ में हारी, पर मिटाई नहीं गई; वो कोल्हापुर से राज करती रही, हुक्मनामे निकालती, ज़मीनें बाँटती, और राजाराम की लाइन की एक टक्कर देती दरबार सजाती रही, भले ही शाहू का सातारा ज़्यादा मशहूर हुआ।

panels.shot: slow pull-back from close-up of Tarabai’s aged face to show Deccan landscape through a window
panels.action: An older Tarabai, lines of age but eyes still sharp, sits by a window; beyond her shoulder, the Deccan hills roll away under clear light, dotted with forts that once echoed with war drums.

dialogue.text: Later memories would praise Peshwas and great generals, yet behind their rise lay years when a widowed regent held the Maratha state together. Tarabai’s courage served a larger duty, and by endurance she outlasted an emperor’s last campaign.

i18n.hi: बाद की यादें पेशवाओं और महा सेनानायकों का गुणगान करेंगी, पर उनकी नींव में वो साल छिपे हैं जब एक विधवा संरक्षक ने मराठा राज्य को जोड़े रखा। तराबाई का साहस एक बड़ी सेवा था, और धीरज से उसने सम्राट की आख़िरी मुहिम से लंबा जीवन पाया।

subtitle_i18n.en: A queen’s resolve against an emperor’s last march
subtitle_i18n.hi: एक महारानी बनाम सम्राट की आख़िरी चढ़ाई
